nodes.summary: Let $\pi(t) = \max(0, \min(1, t))$ clamp a real number $t$ to $[0, 1]$. For every continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ and every bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$, the kernel integrand $(x, t) \mapsto k(x, \pi(t)) \, f(\pi(t))$ is jointly continuous on $[0, 1] \times \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Joint continuity of the kernel integrand

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a finite set of indices and, for $i \in s$, let $\varphi_i$ and $\psi_i$ be bounded continuous functions on $[0, 1]$. If a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ satisfies $k(x, y) = \sum_{i \in s} \varphi_i(x) \psi_i(y)$ for all $x, y \in [0, 1]$, then the range of the integral operator $K$ on the space of bounded continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$, given by…
nodes.title: Separable kernels give finite-rank integral operators

nodes.summary: For every continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, the integral operator $K$ on the space of bounded continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$, given by $(Kf)(x) = \int_0^1 k(x, t) f(t) \, dt$, is a compact operator.
nodes.title: Integral operators with continuous kernels are compact

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a bounded continuous function on $[0, 1]$ and let $\tilde f(s) = f(\max(0, \min(1, s)))$ for real $s$ be its clamped extension. Then $\tilde f(t) = f(t)$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The clamped extension agrees with the function on $(0, 1)$

nodes.summary: For every bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$, the clamped extension $t \mapsto f(\max(0, \min(1, t)))$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the clamped extension

nodes.summary: For a bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$, its clamped extension is the function $\tilde f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $\tilde f(t) = f(\max(0, \min(1, t)))$. Thus $\tilde f(t) = f(0)$ for $t < 0$, $\tilde f(t) = f(t)$ for $t \in [0, 1]$, and $\tilde f(t) = f(1)$ for $t > 1$.
nodes.title: Clamped extension

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(t) = \max(0, \min(1, t))$ clamp a real number $t$ to $[0, 1]$. For every continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, every bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$ and every $x \in [0, 1]$, the function $t \mapsto k(x, \pi(t)) \, f(\pi(t))$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the kernel integrand in $t$

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(t) = \max(0, \min(1, t))$ clamp a real number $t$ to $[0, 1]$. For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, a bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$ and a point $x \in [0, 1]$, the kernel integrand is the function $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $t \mapsto k(x, \pi(t)) \, f(\pi(t))$.
nodes.title: Kernel integrand

nodes.summary: Write $\|\cdot\|$ for the sup norm. For every continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ and every bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$, the function $Kf$ given by $(Kf)(x) = \int_0^1 k(x, t) f(t) \, dt$ satisfies $\|Kf\| \le \|k\| \, \|f\|$.
nodes.title: Sup-norm bound for the integral operator with continuous kernel

nodes.summary: For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, this is the $\mathbb{R}$-linear map $K$ from the space of bounded continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$ to itself given by $(Kf)(x) = \int_0^1 k(x, t) f(t) \, dt$ for $x \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The integral operator with continuous kernel, as a linear map

nodes.summary: For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, write $T_k$ for the integral operator with kernel $k$ on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$. For all continuous kernels $k_1$ and $k_2$, the operator with the pointwise sum kernel is the sum of the operators: $T_{k_1 + k_2} = T_{k_1} + T_{k_2}$.
nodes.title: The integral operator is additive in the kernel

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(t) = \max(0, \min(1, t))$ be the projection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $[0, 1]$. For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, write $T_k$ for the integral operator with kernel $k$ on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$. For every $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ and every $x \in [0, 1]$,
nodes.title: Evaluation formula for the integral operator

nodes.summary: For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, write $T_k$ for the integral operator with kernel $k$ on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$. For every real number $c$ and every continuous kernel $k$, $T_{c k} = c\, T_k$.
nodes.title: The integral operator is homogeneous in the kernel

nodes.summary: The integral operator on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ whose kernel is the zero function on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ is the zero operator.
nodes.title: The zero kernel gives the zero operator

nodes.summary: For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, the integral operator $T_k$ with kernel $k$ is the continuous linear operator on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ given, for $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ and $x \in [0, 1]$, by $(T_k f)(x) = \int_0^1 k(x, t)\, f(t)\, dt$.
nodes.title: Integral operator with a continuous kernel

nodes.summary: $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ denotes the space of bounded continuous functions $[0, 1] \to \mathbb{R}$, with the supremum norm $\|f\| = \sup_{x \in [0, 1]} |f(x)|$.
nodes.title: Continuous functions on the unit interval

nodes.summary: A continuous kernel is a bounded continuous function $k : [0, 1] \times [0, 1] \to \mathbb{R}$. These kernels form a normed space under the supremum norm $\|k\| = \sup_{x, y \in [0, 1]} |k(x, y)|$.
nodes.title: Continuous kernels on the unit square

nodes.summary: For every continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ and every $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$, the kernel value of $k$ and $f$, the function $x \mapsto \int_0^1 k(x, t)\, f(t)\, dt$ on $[0, 1]$, is continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity of the kernel value

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(t) = \max(0, \min(1, t))$ be the projection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $[0, 1]$. For a continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, a function $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ and a point $x \in [0, 1]$, the kernel value is the real number
nodes.title: Kernel value

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(t) = \max(0, \min(1, t))$ be the projection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $[0, 1]$. For every $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ and every $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the clamped extension $f \circ \pi$ of $f$ satisfies $|f(\pi(t))| \le \|f\|$, where $\|f\|$ is the supremum norm.
nodes.title: The clamped extension is bounded by the supremum norm

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a continuous kernel on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, let $K$ be the integral operator with kernel $k$ on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$, let $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$, and let $x, x' \in [0, 1]$ and $\delta \in \mathbb{R}$. If $|k(x, y) - k(x', y)| \le \delta$ for every $y \in [0, 1]$, then $|(Kf)(x) - (Kf)(x')| \le \delta \, \|f\|_\infty$.
nodes.title: Difference bound for the values of a kernel operator

nodes.summary: For every continuous kernel $k$ on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, the integral operator $K$ with kernel $k$ on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ has operator norm $\|K\| \le \|k\|_\infty$.
nodes.title: Norm bound for a kernel integral operator

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a continuous kernel on $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ and let $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$. For every $x \in [0, 1]$, the integral $\int_0^1 k(x, t) \, f(t) \, dt$ has absolute value at most $\|k\|_\infty \, \|f\|_\infty$.
nodes.title: Pointwise bound for a kernel integral

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
